items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: 2,700+ names deleted in Gadarpur on objections filed by poll officers after the deadline
items.claim: Form 10 records published by Uttarakhand's Chief Electoral Officer show that Gadarpur's Electoral Registration Officer and ten Assistant Electoral Registration Officers filed 2,742 Form 7 objections on two dates, 763 on 18 September and 1,979 on 28 September, Newslaundry reported on 2 November. Claims and objections had closed on 13 August, and the final roll was published on 3 October. Rule 17 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 requires an objection lodged after the period to be rejected. By the same records, objections against 4,785 names were filed by 13 August and against 2,825 after it, and the other 83 late objections were filed by individuals, 27 of them dated 14 August by a BJP leader. Of the 5,505 names deleted in Gadarpur after the draft, 2,496 followed objections by the assistant registration officers, 240 objections by the registration officer and 240 objections by private persons, and 2,529 were deleted with no objection recorded against them. Newslaundry met at least 15 deleted electors who said they learnt of it only after the final roll was published. Some said they had received a notice and others that they had received none, and all said officials told them to file Form 6 again. The registration officer, Amrita Sharma, told Newslaundry that officers had not known a Form 7 also had to be generated for electors marked absent, and that by the time this was noticed the hearings were over.
items.quote: Both dates fell more than a month after the claims and objections period ended on August 13, with the second batch just logged five days before the final electoral roll was published.
items.response: The registration officer said the late filings were a delay in generating the forms on the system, that hearings had already been held, and that these were Form 7 deletions on anomaly notices, which she distinguished from an officer's own proceedings under rule 21A. She said about 52,000 notices were issued in Gadarpur and about 45,000 electors heard and kept on the roll, that not a single name was deleted without a notice, and that the same ten assistant officers who filed the objections held the hearings. She said only forms submitted by 13 August were accepted and that the entries dated 14 August were uploads made late that night. On two electors who say they gave the documents asked for or had no notice, she said she would have to examine the records. She said more than 1,800 Form 6 applications had been received since the revision, over 900 of them from electors deleted for absence or other reasons. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission.
items.note: First reading, 10 November 2026. By Ashwine Kumar Singh and Basant Kumar in Newslaundry, published 2 November 2026 at 10:00 am IST (datePublished 2026-11-02T04:30:00Z), read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 10 November 2026. 763 and 1,979 make 2,742, and with the 83 make 2,825. 2,496, 240, 240 and 2,529 make 5,505, which is the count of names deleted after the draft in Gadarpur on the site's Uttarakhand constituency table. items.headline: Thousands of votes marked for deletion in Andhra Pradesh without reasons on record
items.claim: The News Minute found that 40,006 electors were named for deletion in Form 7 applications in Andhra Pradesh between 29 September and 10 October, the last 12 days of claims and objections, and that 20,959 of them had an Electoral Registration Officer or an Assistant Electoral Registration Officer named as the objector in the Commission's consolidated Form 10 statements. Where an ordinary elector is the objector the statements give a reason, and where an officer is named they give none. In the 20 constituencies with the most names sought for deletion, officers were the objectors for 16,241 of 21,115. In Chandragiri the assistant officer is named 1,991 times and the officer 6 times among 2,452 names, in Palacole the officer 311 times and the assistant officer 1,701 times among 2,220, in Ongole the officer 1,277 times among 1,712, and in Narsapuram 1,369 times among 1,450. TNM could not read the statements from before 29 September, because each stays online for a week. The report sets out that rule 13(2) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 lets only an elector on the roll object to an entry, and that section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and rule 21A let the officer delete a name of his own motion after giving the elector a chance to be heard. Two registration officers and an assistant officer told TNM that the ERO-NET software shows no reason once the officer's login marks an elector ineligible, which generates the Form 7, and that it allows deletions to be uploaded in bulk.
items.quote: We noticed that when Form 7s are filed by normal citizens, the consolidated statement carries the reason for objection. But the reason for objection is not listed when an ERO or AERO is the objector.
items.response: TNM sent questions to Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, and had no reply when it published. The Chief Electoral Officer answered on 28 October that the forms were generated through the software on the Commission's instructions for electors found ineligible after notices (form7-65). One registration officer told TNM that the officer is never in fact the objector, that the request comes from a family member or a booth level agent, and that his office holds documents to show it.

items.headline: Andhra CEO says no independent deletions. TNM’s questions about transparency remain
items.claim: Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer answered TNM's report on Form 7s naming officers as objectors (form7-64) on 28 October, in a thread on the office's X account that says no registration officer or assistant registration officer deleted any name of his own motion. The thread says booth level officers found 44,89,512 electors not at their addresses between 15 June and 24 July 2026, and the draft roll of 31 July held 3,71,38,182 electors. Officers then sent notices to electors with no mapping or with data anomalies, and by 23 October another 1,73,701 electors had been found ineligible for the final roll. For each of them, the thread says, the officer passed a speaking order giving the reasons and uploaded it to ECINET, the booth level officer delivered the order to the elector with notice of an appeal to the District Collector, and a Form 7 was generated through ECINET in the officer's name as the Commission instructs, because a deletion takes effect in the system only after a Form 7 is generated. It calls the report's insinuations of procedural violations baseless and misleading and condemns them. The News Minute replied the same day that the statement does not say why officers appear as objectors in the published records or why no reason is shown in those cases.
items.quote: For deletion of all such electors, Form-7 have been auto-generated by the ERO / AERO through ECI-Net technically as per the ECI instructions.
items.response: The thread is the Chief Electoral Officer's own reply. TNM says its report did not allege that officers deleted names without due process, and that its question was why the public records give no reason for the deletions officers are named in. The thread does not say how many of the 20,959 electors in TNM's count are among the 1,73,701.

items.headline: As thousands were deleted from electoral rolls using auto-generated Form-7s, ECI gave no SOPs to State Electoral Officers
items.claim: Several State election officials told The Hindu that the Commission's software, ERONet, generated Form 7s automatically when officials deleted electors at the hearings of the revision, and that the forms carried the officers' digital signatures, the paper reported on 15 October. It named Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal as states where officials had used this route to delete electors with unresolved logical discrepancies or with no mapping, and it said other reports had put the names deleted this way at more than 87,000 in Uttar Pradesh and more than 95,000 in Uttarakhand. The paper reported, from sources, that no written communication or standard operating procedure on these forms was shared with the election authorities in the states. It set out that the electoral rules make no provision for a registration officer or an assistant registration officer to file a Form 7, and that the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2024 makes none for the registration officer to file one, though the officer, who decides objections, can delete a name found ineligible. The paper reports that the manual mentions auto-generated Form 7s only in the verification of Photo Similar Entries, where the forms ERONet generates are not filed by the registration officer and must be signed by the booth level officer after a field verification, or the system cannot accept or process them.
items.quote: According to several State electoral officials The Hindu spoke with, the ECI’s software, ERONet, automatically generated these Form 7s when officials deleted voters during the SIR hearings. The auto-generated forms came with the officers’ digital signatures.
items.response: The paper reported that the Commission had yet to answer an official query on the matter. Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said on 28 October that the forms in that state were generated through ECINET in the officers' names as the Commission instructs, for electors found ineligible after a notice and a speaking order (form7-65). Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer's office called the account of such forms in that state misleading on 13 October, and said notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders came before any action (up-02).
items.note: First reading, 11 November 2026. items.headline: Delhi SIR: Why BJP BLAs’ voter deletion applications in Mustafabad focused on three neighbourhoods
items.claim: The 796 Form 7 applications that name 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP as objectors in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency are mostly concentrated in 25 of its 294 polling booths, in the neighbourhoods of Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur and Chandu Nagar, The Hindu reported on 10 November. The paper reports that all of them are against Muslim electors and that they are over 76% of the 1,044 deletion applications received in the constituency up to 4 November, from the published data. The applications give absence, a permanent shift or death as the reason, and the paper found at least 87 of the electors named living at their registered addresses. The paper reports, from an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers, that the 25 booths appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population and, by the workers' claims, few names left off the draft roll. BJP leaders who spoke to it on condition of anonymity said that after the draft of 31 August party workers compared the number of names placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors in booths with a majority of Muslim electors and in booths with a majority of Hindu electors, prepared lists of Muslim electors, which the paper says it saw, and then concentrated on the 25 booths, where the agents began filing from the first week of October. The paper says it found copies of these booths' rolls, with the names of Muslim electors marked on them, with BJP workers in the area. It reports that the Commission's booth-wise figures do not bear out the workers' claim. By its count, names left off the draft averaged 274 a booth in Mustafabad and reached 538 at the most, and in most of the 25 booths they were close to the average. Parts 108 and 129, which it counts among the five booths with the fewest names left off the draft, carry 35 and 37 of the agents' applications. No application names a BJP agent in the other three, which BJP workers said were mostly Hindu. Nehru Vihar has the most applications, 496. The paper reports that none of the Form 7s received in Mustafabad came with the undertaking an agent must give.
items.quote: The Form 7 applications were all against Muslim electors, and the 25 booths, spread across three neighbourhoods, appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population with claims of few deletions when the draft electoral roll was published as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers showed.
items.response: The Delhi BJP spokesperson, Praveen Shankar Kapoor, told the paper that the party's agents had not filed any Form 7s in Mustafabad, that the party had not directed any forms to be filed, and that booth level officers and the Commission would act on any objections under the rules. The BJP councillor for Nehru Vihar, Arun Bhati, said he was not authorised to speak about the applications, and said that some booths in Mustafabad had 300 to 500 votes deleted, which he said were coincidentally of Hindu voters, while others had fewer than 100, and that the two could not both be correct. The paper reports that officials maintain religious identity has no role in verification. The agent named in 57 applications told the paper he had filed them himself because the electors had shifted, and the councillor's brother, an agent named in 37, denied filing his. The report does not say how the paper established the religion of the electors or of each booth's population.

items.headline: Form 7 withdrawals, rejections follow Maharashtra scrutiny on false objections
items.claim: Amit Sanap, the electoral registration officer for Bhiwandi East, told the Hindustan Times that his office had received 540 Form 7 applications seeking deletions in the constituency and had rejected over 450 of them, because the electors the forms said were not living at their addresses were found living there. The paper reports that political parties' booth level agents filed 480 of the 540 and that some applicants could face criminal action for false information. Sanap said some applicants had withdrawn their applications and that action would begin once the formal orders were prepared. The paper reports that Form 7s filed by agents and private complainants have been withdrawn or rejected in large numbers on scrutiny in Mumbai and the constituencies around it, after Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer told registration officers to place the burden of proof on the objector, to summon objectors and verify their claims before acting, and to begin criminal action against false filings. A senior state election official told the paper that objectors are allowed to withdraw, and that withdrawals began once action started and the first FIR was registered in Dharavi three weeks earlier (form7-55). With claims and objections due to close on Friday, 13 November, the Commission had received over 23 lakh forms for additions, deletions and corrections in Maharashtra, more than 95,000 of them Form 7s, the paper reports.

items.headline: Their addresses changed without consent. Then their voter names vanished
items.claim: The Pune District Election Officer, Suhas Diwase, wrote to Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, S Chockalingam, on 17 October 2024 that a large number of electors in the district were being shifted to other constituencies through Form 8 applications for a change of address, that many of the applications gave the same electricity bill as proof of the new address in a name that did not match the elector's, and that many came from a single IP address, The Indian Express reported on 14 November from documents it reviewed. The paper reports that one of two later letters suggested the applications were being submitted in bulk by persons other than the electors. In the first of them, on 20 March 2025, his successor, Jitendra Dudi, wrote that the electors had been found living where they were and had not shifted. In the second, on 4 April 2025, he wrote that when a Form 8 is approved in the new constituency the ERONET software generates a Form 7 for deletion in the old one, which the registration officer there can only accept, and he asked for an option to reject it. On 19 November 2025 Ajit Gavhane, who contested Bhosari for the NCP (Sharad Pawar) in the 2024 Assembly election, gave the Chief Electoral Officer's office a list of 58 electors of Bhosari who, he said, had never applied to be moved or deleted, and the office ordered an inquiry the next day. The Bhosari registration officer reported that one of the 58 had been moved within the constituency and that the other 57 were among 5,603 electors for whom a Form 7 had been generated automatically after an address change was accepted in another constituency. The reports of the Pimpri and Khadakvasla registration officers and of the Thane District Election Officer, which the Pune District Election Officer sent on with his reply of 27 January 2026, said the address changes had been accepted on the documents submitted without a field check by a booth level officer, and the other five reports said the check had been done. After the paper's queries, the District Election Officer directed on 31 October 2026 that action be taken against those responsible and issued a show-cause notice to the Pimpri registration officer. On 1 November the Pimpri assistant registration officer filed a non-cognizable offence report at Nigdi police station under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, against the persons who used four mobile numbers to file 40 Form 8 applications. The paper reports that the District Election Officer found that three of the 58 had died and 11 were living where they were registered, and that Form 6 applications had been filed online to bring the other 43 back onto Bhosari's roll. Dudi told Hindustan Times, in its report of 15 November, that 60 electors of Bhosari had been moved without their knowledge before the 2024 Lok Sabha election, that two of them had since died, and that the other 58 had been added back to the roll after filing Form 6.
items.quote: The remaining 57 figured among the 5,603 voters, for whom Form 7 (the form for deleting a voter) had been automatically generated after address change applications were submitted and accepted at some other constituency.
items.response: Chockalingam told The Indian Express that an option to reject the generated Form 7 was not feasible because it would leave an elector registered in two constituencies at once, and that bulk filing had been addressed by the Aadhaar-based digital signature the Commission made mandatory in September 2025. The Pune District Election Officer's reply of 27 January 2026 said that a very large number of applications had been received during the 2024 election period and had to be decided within the time set so that the roll could be printed for the Assembly election. The paper reports that the Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote to the Pune District Election Officer asking for an explanation and the action taken on 2 November, the day the paper sent its query. Gavhane claimed more than 15,000 such cases, and the paper reports that the person who prepared his list called it a representative list. Dudi told Hindustan Times that the case at Nigdi was against one person who had submitted all the Form 8 applications, and that his office was gathering details of that person's background. Neither report names the person.

items.headline: ECI yet to generate forms for 20.6 million deleted Maharashtra voters, likely to miss final roll revision deadline
items.claim: Ten days after the Commission's letter of 6 November, fresh enumeration forms had not yet been generated on ECINET for the 20.60 million electors left off Maharashtra's draft roll of 31 August, Hindustan Times reported on 16 November. The paper gives 7.54 million of them as absent, 7.67 million as permanently shifted, 3.48 million as dead, 1.76 million as registered at more than one polling station and 2,22,390 as other. It reports that the Commission said the forms would be sent by WhatsApp, SMS or calls or delivered in person by booth level officers, and that without the forms the booth level officers and registration officers have been unable to reach these electors. The paper reports that the Commission asked an elector who has not moved to fill Annexure B and one who has moved to give the new address in Annexure C, and that no last date has been set for either. Officials told the paper that the revision was likely to be delayed further. One of them said that the final roll would not be published on 30 November as scheduled. Another said that there was no last date for bringing these electors back, and that distributing, collecting and digitising the forms would take a few weeks and the revision would be extended again. The paper reports that the letter of 6 November is understood to have been issued to meet the Commission's assurance to the Supreme Court, which is hearing petitions against the deletions in Maharashtra, that these electors would be given another opportunity.
items.quote: It is expected to take much longer, as even the pre-filled enumeration forms have not yet been generated.
items.response: The report gives no response from the Commission or from the office of Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, and none of the officials is named. One official told the paper that the Commission could have asked the electors marked absent to file Form 6 and those marked shifted to file Form 8. Sandesh Kondvilkar, a general secretary of the Congress in Maharashtra, told the paper that the process so far had been an "eyewash". He alleged that in many cases booth level officers had marked electors absent without visiting their addresses, and said that the enumeration forms and Annexures B and C were not yet being accepted on the ground and that the final roll would now be postponed.

items.headline: Karnataka High Court stays probe against 10 more persons accused of attempting to delete Muslim voters through Form 7
items.claim: Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde of the Karnataka High Court on 17 November 2026 stayed further investigation in three more FIRs against BJP booth level agents over bulk Form 7 applications, Bar and Bench, LiveLaw and Hindustan Times reported. LiveLaw gives the three FIRs as one at the Narasimharaja police station in Mysuru against three agents, one at the Jayanagar police station in Bengaluru against two and one at the Shanivarasante police station in Kodagu against five, ten petitioners in all. With them the Court has stayed the investigation in five cases. In the two Malleshwaram cases (form7-48) the orders defer the State's applications to vacate the stays of 9 October and stay further investigation until further orders. Each order says that the inquiry by the registration officer under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 has to run its course first, and that the officer's finding may give the material to decide whether an FIR should be quashed or investigated. In the Malleshwaram and Jayanagar orders the Court said that the agents had not disowned their signatures on the forms and that the allegation of forgery could not be accepted at that stage. In those three cases and in Kodagu the Court directed the Election Commission, a respondent in each, to place on record the materials on its decisions on the Form 7 applications the agents filed. In the Mysuru case it directed the petitioners to add the State Election Commission as a respondent and directed that respondent to place the same materials on record. The complaints, as Bar and Bench and Hindustan Times report them, allege that the applications carried false information, forged signatures or impersonation, and some of them allege that the applications were aimed at Muslim electors. Bar and Bench gives the complaints' counts as 778 applications across eight polling stations in Malleshwaram, 5,698 applications in Jayanagar, 4,327 of them in Gurrappanapalya ward, 136 electors in Yeshwanthpur and 64 in Kodagu.
items.quote: The Court is of the view inquiry under the Rules, 1960, has to run its course to ascertain whether the petitioners have furnished correct information.
items.response: The Advocate General, K Shashi Kiran Shetty, opposed the petitions for the State and argued that fake or forged applications could not be permitted during the revision, because the right to vote is a valuable right. The petitioners argued that booth level agents were entitled to file Form 7 objections for political parties and that the registration officer had to examine whether the objections were correct. The Court allowed the complainants to seek modification or vacation of the interim orders, and the State to seek modification once it receives the Commission's records, Bar and Bench reported. No next date was reported.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: ECI Bends Its Own Rules to Bring Back Deleted Voters
items.claim: Delhi's Deputy Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Commission's headquarters asking how to carry out its order that electors left off Delhi's draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate may return through a fresh enumeration form with an annexure, The Reporters' Collective reported on 20 November. Under the order an elector who has moved within Delhi adds the new address in an annexure to the enumeration form and does not file Form 8. The Collective reported that the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer told the Commission that printing and sorting the regenerated forms would take at least a month, and that many electors were asking whether they could download their forms with their old EPIC numbers when no such provision existed in ECINET. The part of the letter the Collective shows says the enquiries were reaching the office's 1950 call centre, that "as on date no such provision exists in ECINET", and asks the Commission, whose IT team maintains ECINET, to provide for electors to download or fill their forms on ECINET or the website. It reported that the office asked for changes to ECINET so that the EPIC numbers of these electors could be brought back into the database and the forms downloaded online, to the BLO app so that booth level officers could hand out the forms, verify the details and process the cases, and to the portal of the registration officers so that they could take final decisions on these electors. The Collective says the route was needed because the EPIC numbers of electors in the absent, shifted, dead or duplicate list had been deleted from the database, and an elector needs one to file Form 8. It gives 47.6 lakh electors left off the draft, 43 lakh of them marked shifted or absent, and the Commission's timeline as enumeration forms decided by 10 December and the final roll published by 22 December. It also reports informal WhatsApp instructions sent to booth level officers in the last week of October, which it saw, asking them to obtain the lists for their booths, revisit the addresses of the electors they had marked missing and bring back those they found through Form 6. The Commission wrote on 3 November that no action was to be started against an elector only because the elector was on an earlier roll and had filed Form 6, and the Collective reports that the order for regenerated enumeration forms came three days later.
items.quote: The Delhi CEO office wrote to the ECI, pointing out that printing and sorting through these forms “will take at least a month.”
items.response: The Collective reports that its questions to the Commission and to the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer on how the changes would be made had not been answered. The report does not date the letter, name the Deputy Chief Electoral Officer or say whether the Commission has replied. Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer said in a press note of 17 November that an elector can fill the form on the Commission's website or the ECINET app with the EPIC number held before the name was left off, and the report does not say whether the letter came before or after that note.

items.headline: SIR: Telangana Gets Only 9 Enumeration Forms
items.claim: Only nine enumeration forms had been received across Telangana from electors left off the draft roll of 17 August as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, nearly a fortnight after the Commission directed officials to accept them, Deccan Chronicle reported on 19 November. items.headline: झारखंड में मतदाता सूची पुनरीक्षण: 41 लाख मामलों का निष्पादन, 8 लाख लंबित
items.claim: Of 45,49,961 logical discrepancy cases in Jharkhand, 41,03,251, or 90.18 per cent, had been disposed of by 19 November and 4,46,710 were pending, and of 14,03,981 no-mapping cases 10,42,976, or 74.29 per cent, had been disposed of and 3,61,005 were pending, Amar Ujala reported from official figures. Dainik Jagran gives the same figures from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer. Lohardaga and West Singhbhum had disposed of every case in both categories and updated them on the ECINET app. Sahibganj had disposed of the smallest share, 76.36 per cent of its discrepancy cases and 55.69 per cent of its no-mapping cases, against 77.89 and 57.96 per cent in Pakur and 85.09 and 58.67 per cent in Jamtara, and Palamu had disposed of 56.65 per cent of its no-mapping cases. Dainik Jagran reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, told district and registration officers in a video conference on Thursday, 19 November, that electors on the draft roll who had been sent notices and had not yet given documents were to be visited at home to collect them, and that electors on the absent, shifted, dead or duplicate list were to be contacted again to fill enumeration forms. Dainik Jagran credits the progress to camps it calls 'one more chance' camps, held at all polling stations on Tuesday. Live Hindustan reported on 19 November that 9,46,954 Form 6 applications, 128 Form 6A, 1,50,007 Form 7 and 5,86,762 Form 8 had been digitised in the state so far.

items.headline: SIR: Hatia, Daltonganj face rising voter verification pressure
items.claim: The Times of India reported from the bulletin the Chief Electoral Officer's office issued on Friday that 5,585 Form 7 objections were digitised across Jharkhand on Thursday, 19 November, taking the total to 1,75,398. Ranchi district accounted for 1,666 of the day's objections, Palamu for 1,049 and Giridih for 906, together nearly 65% of the day's total. Among constituencies Daltonganj had the most that day, 991, followed by Hatia with 869, Bagodar 579, Kodarma 496, Tamar 479, Simdega 353 and Kanke 300. The Commission's scrutiny data for Thursday showed 28,047 cases unresolved in Hatia across the no-mapping, logical discrepancy and other categories, and 27,773 in Daltonganj. The paper reports the largest backlogs in Seraikela, 39,589, and Bokaro, 31,238, which recorded one and five fresh Form 7 objections that day. Across the state 10,587 applications on Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 were digitised on Thursday, taking the total to 17.21 lakh. The Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, said the daily Form 7 figures include both objections and forms generated automatically when electors are shifted between polling stations. The paper reports that on an inspection in Jharia on Friday he found lapses in verification, among them eligible voters left out although they had documents, and ordered officials to complete the hearings, to issue Form 6 to those turning 18 by 1 October 2026 and to include all eligible voters.
items.quote: Kumar clarified that the daily Form 7 figures include both objections and auto-generated forms created when electors are shifted between polling stations.
items.response: The figures are the Chief Electoral Officer's office's as the paper reports them, and the bulletin itself was not read. items.headline: Maharashtra SIR: On BJP seat, 14,567 voter deletion requests were filed; only 74 found valid
items.claim: In the Bhusawal Assembly constituency of Jalgaon district, 14,567 Form 7 objections seeking deletions were received by post, and after an inquiry by booth level officers only 74 electors were found eligible for deletion, The Indian Express reported on 21 November from the factual report prepared after the inquiry. The report says 21 objectors withdrew 2,532 objections in writing. For the rest, notices were issued to the objectors and a public notice published in the newspaper on 5 November asked them to submit evidence, and booth level officers inspected and inquired into each application on the spot. By the order of 17 November of the Sub-Divisional Officer, who is the Electoral Registration Officer, all 14,567 objections were disposed of. Action has begun on the 74 as the rules require, and the paper reports that the district administration has begun legal action against those who filed objections with malicious intent. The paper's opening says 186 people had sought the deletion of 14,562 voters. The seat is held by the BJP's Sanjay Savkare, Maharashtra's Minister for Textiles. A Congress booth level agent who first raised the bulk filing told the paper that many of the people named as objectors denied having signed the forms, and asked for a detailed inquiry. A senior official in the state Chief Electoral Officer's office said the forms came by post, so all were accepted because there was no way of knowing who the objector was, and that after hearings and the disposal of malicious objections only 74 were accepted.
items.quote: A total of 14,567 objections were received by post in Form No. 7 in the 12-Bhusawal Assembly Constituency. Out of the above, 21 objectors have voluntarily withdrawn 2,532 objections through written applications.
items.response: The figures are the factual report's and the registration officer's order's, as the paper quotes them. The report does not say who the objectors were, against whom the objections were filed, or when they were sent. No reply from the minister or the BJP was reported.

items.headline: Over 6 Lakh Voter Names Deleted in Telangana Since Jan. 1 via Form-7; Opacity Over 79 Lakh Pleas Sparks Row
items.claim: More than 6 lakh names had been deleted from Telangana's rolls through Form 7 since 1 January by Saturday, 21 November, Deccan Chronicle reported on 22 November. The paper reports that about 5 lakh names had been deleted from 1 January before the intensive revision began, and that more than one lakh were deleted through Form 7 in the past month. Official sources the paper does not name told it that officials had received 79 lakh Form 7 applications seeking deletion through the year, had rejected 64 lakh of them and kept 8.8 lakh pending. That count is more than 13 times the 5,88,659 Form 7 applications that Telangana Today reported the Chief Electoral Officer's office had recorded from 1 January to 31 October (form7-59), and the paper does not reconcile the two. A senior official told the paper that most of the applications came in the claims and objections period, and would not give a break-up by applicant, the dates of the applications or who was deleted. P. Rajesh Kumar, chairman of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee's Election Commission Coordination Committee, said the party had tried to stop booth level agents from filing false Form 7s, and that the applications outnumbered the electors on the absent, shifted, dead or duplicate list, which he put at 73 lakh. The paper reports that the authorities did not provide the forms filed by booth level agents in the Karimnagar Assembly constituency in answer to an application under the Right to Information Act, and gave instead the details of applications by voters seeking to delete the names of members of their families. The applicant told the paper that after the application was escalated to the collector the authorities gave details of only six members from the entire constituency.
items.quote: According to official sources, poll officials throughout the year had received 79 lakh applications via Form-7 seeking deletion of names. Of these, poll officials rejected 64 lakh applications and kept 8.8 lakh pending.
items.response: The figures come from official sources the paper does not name, and the senior official is not named. The report gives no count for any district, and does not say how the 79 lakh applications were counted.

Telangana Today reported 5,88,659 Form 7 applications recorded from 1 January to 31 October, 5,16,052 accepted, 57,980 rejected and 14,627 pending (form7-59), and The Hindu 5,81,273 filed since 1 January (form7-57). The 79 lakh is more than 13 times those counts and more than the 73,39,235 electors left off Telangana's draft (data/india/states.json), which is the 73 lakh the Congress leader cites. items.headline: ASDD voter review moves at snail’s pace in Hyderabad
items.claim: Of the 19,41,444 electors in Hyderabad district's 15 Assembly constituencies who were left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead, duplicate or other, verification had been completed for 7,69,112, or 39.62 percent, by 20 November, leaving 11,72,332, The New Indian Express reported on 22 November from figures presented at a meeting with representatives of political parties. Of the 13,45,333 electors in the shifted category 4,22,994 had been verified, and of the 2,99,850 absent electors around 1,66,813. Of the 1,56,392 in the dead category 95,198 had been verified and 61,194 were pending, and of the 99,264 duplicates 66,122 had been verified and 33,142 were pending. In the other category around 17,985 of 40,605 electors, or 44.29 percent, had been verified. By 20 November officials had distributed 10 enumeration forms and collected 10, all of them in the shifted category, and the figures for the other categories were zero. In all 1,528 electors on the list had applied afresh on Form 6, 1,077 of them in the shifted category and 420 in the absent category.

items.headline: SIR: Over 18k names likely to be struck out from electoral roll so far; Kodarma, Deoghar account for 27%
items.claim: In Jharkhand 18,425 cases had been marked ineligible for inclusion in the final roll by 21 November, The Times of India reported from the latest data of the Chief Electoral Officer's office. Kodarma had the most, 2,781, and Deoghar 2,293, together 5,074, or around 27.5% of the state's total. Of the 18,425, 9,153 were in the logical discrepancy category, 7,766 in the no-mapping category and 1,506 in the category the data calls other. Of 2,21,19,847 cases in the three categories, 2,13,65,467 had been disposed of as of 21 November, a disposal rate of 96.59%, and 7,54,380 were pending, 3,71,970 of them logical discrepancy cases, 3,11,757 no-mapping cases and 70,653 other. The Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, said cases marked Park for Final would be included in the final roll and cases marked Found Ineligible for Final would not, and told the paper that the number of deletions could increase as officials completed scrutiny of the remaining cases. On an inspection in Deoghar on Saturday, 21 November, he found deficiencies in the verification of documents at hearings at polling stations in Sonaraitharhi block of the Jarmundi constituency, and directed the registration officer and assistant registration officers to correct them and report by 30 November.

items.headline: No voter-deletion forms for BJP workers in UP in this round of electoral roll preparation
items.claim: The BJP has decided not to give Form 7 to its booth level agents in Uttar Pradesh during the special summary revision and is giving them only Form 6 and Form 8, The Indian Express reported on 22 November from sources in the party. The paper reports the decision after complaints from several constituencies of Form 7s filed in bulk during the intensive revision, some of which led to FIRs. Party sources told the paper that the BJP has sent its workers the list of names deleted during the intensive revision as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and that its booth level agents and workers are checking it in door-to-door visits. A senior BJP leader said the party had given its workers in every Assembly seat around 5,000 copies of Form 6 and 1,000 copies of Form 8, with a copy of the roll and the list of deleted names, and that no Form 7 was being provided. On the allegations that its booth level agents had filed Form 7s in bulk, the leader said the forms its workers had submitted were largely not processed. Another leader said that on 22, 23 and 24 November ministers, MPs, MLAs and office-bearers would be at their assigned polling booths for door-to-door contact, as part of the party's month-long Matdata Jodo Abhiyan, whose progress is to be reviewed on 13 December. The paper reports that the draft roll of the summary revision put Uttar Pradesh's electors at 13.58 crore as of 17 November, 18.84 lakh more than the final roll of 10 April, and that claims and objections run till 16 December and the final roll is due on 4 January.
items.quote: No Form 7 is being provided as the party wants to use its energy and human resources towards the inclusion of new and left-out voters.
items.response: The account is the party's, from sources and leaders the paper does not name. The report gives no official count of Form 7s filed in the summary revision, and does not say how many of the forms BJP workers filed during the intensive revision were decided, or how.

The 18.84 lakh agrees with the net rise of 18,84,113 between the final roll of 10 April and the draft of 17 November (data/india/raw/ssr_draft.csv). The paper quotes the Chief Minister's claim about the religion of electors deleted and added during the intensive revision. It is a claim about religion and is not carried. The paper's account of the Commission rejecting the Samajwadi Party president's claims of mass deletions is not carried, because the report gives no date or source for it. Party sources also told the paper that lists are being compiled of people turning 18 by 1 January 2027, women living in their marital homes, people on panchayat rolls and not on the Assembly roll, beneficiaries of government schemes, ration card holders and migrants. These are not carried, because they describe the party's canvassing and give no figures. No leader is named in the report. items.headline: NCP(SP) alleges BJP targeting voters via SIR objections
items.claim: More than 6,300 objections to entries in the draft roll were filed in the Indapur Assembly constituency of Pune district during the intensive revision, The Indian Express reported on 21 November. The Naib Tehsildar at Indapur, Vijay Ghughe, told the paper that 2,120 of them had been withdrawn by the people who filed them. A list of withdrawals he shared showed that 100 sets of applications, filed by 98 people against 2,120 voters, had been withdrawn. He said hearings on the objections were being held at the Tehsildar's office. The paper checked the lists of booth level agents by party against the names of those who withdrew, and found that at least 55 of the 100 sets, accounting for 1,172 objections, had been withdrawn by BJP booth level agents. One of them was listed as an agent of both the BJP and the NCP(SP), and none of the others who withdrew was listed as an agent of any party. items.headline: BJP launches voter enrolment drive in UP, warns cadres against ‘intruders’
items.claim: The BJP's president in Uttar Pradesh, Pankaj Chaudhary, told PTI on Sunday, 22 November, that the party's workers had been briefed to use Form 6 to add eligible electors left off the roll during the summary revision and Form 8 to correct entries or record a change of residence. PTI reports that the workers have also been asked to keep watch against 'ghuspaithiyas', a word PTI glosses as intruders, and it quotes Chaudhary as saying that the party's stand on 'ghuspaithiyas' is clear and that, if required, Form 7 will be used towards that objective. Chaudhary took part the same day in the party's three-day voter enrolment drive, which began on Sunday, at Faizullahganj in Lucknow, where PTI quotes him telling people to use Form 6 to add names and Form 7 to object to suspect entries. The Times of India reported on 23 November that the party has given its district chiefs the task of adding 10,000 to 15,000 names 'in each of the state's 402 assembly constituencies' through house visits, and that the party's block head at Behrampur in Ghaziabad said its workers were handing out Forms 6, 7 and 8 and working with the booth level officers of their areas. The paper reports that 18.8 lakh names have been added to the roll through the summary revision so far, around 61,000 of them in Ghaziabad. The draft roll of 17 November held 18,84,113 more electors than the final roll of 10 April, which is a net rise.
items.quote: But surely the party’s stand on ‘ghuspaithiyas’ is clear and towards this objective, if required, Form 7 will be used,

items.headline: Pakur’s SIR docu checks under lens over birth cert discrepancy
items.claim: The Times of India reported on 23 November that a letter of 22 November from the medical officer in charge of the community health centre at Barharwa in Sahibganj district to the civil surgeon says 'the Union govt did not issue' a birth certificate dated 17 May 2026 in the name of a woman whose parents are reported to live in Pakur district. The paper gives the letter as saying that the civil registration system portal 'was not open at the Union govt on that date', that no certificate was issued through it and that a search of the portal for the date returned no records. The certificate gives 17 May as both its date of registration and its date of issue and names the Barharwa health centre as the registering institution. The paper says it remains to be established whether the certificate was submitted at a hearing of the revision and who produced it. The discrepancy came to light on Sunday, 22 November, as the Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, reviewed the revision in the Rajmahal and Pakur constituencies. The Times of India quotes him as saying that no elector would be deleted without due procedure, including two notices, a hearing, physical verification and a reasoned final order. In Pakur he found electors on the draft roll who had not given the documents asked for, and he asked applicants who had moved from West Bengal and whose documents were pending there to give their present registration officers the acknowledgements of their applications so that officials in Jharkhand could take it up with those in West Bengal. Dainik Jagran reports that registration officers in Pakur had sent notices to many such people while their documents were being prepared in West Bengal, that officials in Rajmahal told him many people in the Diyara area have no khatiyan and so cannot get residence or caste certificates, and that the Commission is concerned at the slow progress of the revision in Rajmahal. The Times of India reports that as of 19 November Sahibganj had disposed of 55.69% of its no-mapping cases and Pakur 57.96%, and that the two districts together had 99,025 no-mapping and logical discrepancy cases pending.

items.response: The letter was not read, and the paper does not say who gave it the letter or what step the civil surgeon or the registration officer has taken on it. Neither report says how many electors in Pakur were sent notices while their documents were pending in West Bengal.

items.headline: Post SIR, Jharkhand final electoral roll likely to list 2.33 crore voters: CEO
items.claim: Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, told The Times of India on Monday, 23 November, that he expected the final roll, due on 22 December, to hold around 2.33 crore electors, including the 9 to 10 lakh names likely to be added during the revision, and that deletions after the revision could be around 33 lakh. The paper gives around 2.64 crore electors on the roll before the revision began on 30 June and around 2.21 crore on the draft of 5 August. It reports from the bulletin of 23 November that 17,56,325 applications had been digitised in the state, 9,64,306 on Form 6, 136 on Form 6A, 1,96,853 on Form 7 and 5,95,030 on Form 8, and that 13,114 were digitised on 22 November alone, 8,837 of them on Form 7. At a review by video conference the same day he told district election officers and registration officers that super checks had found fake birth certificates attached in cases in Garhwa, Ranchi and Palamu, and that one more was found in Pakur during his inspection of 22 November. He directed them to verify the eligibility of applicants, to take legal action against those who submit fake birth certificates and those who help to provide them, to record the names and EPIC numbers of applicants' parents where these are on the rolls, and to complete super checks and send compliance reports by 30 November. He said that no elector on the draft roll should be deleted without a proper inquiry, a reasoned order and due process. He added that no further special camps are planned.
items.quote: The total number of name deletions after the SIR could be around 33 lakh, state chief electoral officer (CEO) K Ravi Kumar said on Monday.
items.response: The 2.33 crore and the 33 lakh are the Chief Electoral Officer's expectations, and the paper says the precise calculation behind the projected additions, deletions and final electorate awaits the final roll. items.headline: Delhi Congress alleges 75 living voters shown as dead on Form 7 in Mustafabad
items.claim: The Delhi Congress alleged on Monday, 23 November, that 75 living electors in Mustafabad had been classified as dead in Form 7 applications during the revision, and demanded an impartial inquiry, PTI reported. The party's Delhi president, Devender Yadav, told a press conference at Rajiv Bhawan that the party's booth level agent had identified 65 of the 75 as alive during door-to-door verification in the Nehru Vihar ward of the constituency. The party said 16 of the electors attended the press conference with their voter identity cards. Yadav alleged that booth level agents appointed by the BJP had misused Form 7 to show living electors as dead, asked the Commission to make clear who had given the authority to do so, and demanded special hearings for the electors and action against those found responsible. He also questioned the transfer of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, during the revision.
items.quote: According to the complaints received by the Delhi Congress, Form 7 has been misused to declare living persons as dead.
items.response: PTI reports no immediate response from Delhi's election office or the BJP. The figures are the party's. The report does not say when the applications were filed, whether they are among those The Hindu counted (form7-67), or whether any of the 75 names has been deleted.

items.case: Writ petition by four petitioners to quash the Suddaguntepalya police FIR of 7 October over Form 7 applications, W.P. No. 32768 of 2026, Karnataka High Court (form7-42, form7-75)
items.headline: Karnataka High Court Refuses To Stay Form 7 Voter Deletion Probe, Bars Arrest Of Petitioners
items.claim: Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde of the Karnataka High Court declined on 20 November 2026 to stay the police investigation into an FIR over Form 7 applications filed to delete six electors from the roll in Bengaluru, and directed that the petitioners not be arrested and that no chargesheet be filed without the Court's leave, LawChakra and Bar and Bench reported. The Suddaguntepalya police registered the FIR on 7 October against the Jayanagar MLA of the BJP, C K Ramamurthy, and three others, under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and sections 217(b), 3(5), 336(2), 340(2) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. The complainant alleges that Form 7 applications were filed to delete his name and those of five members of his family, who have lived at Old Gurappanapalya in Bengaluru for about 50 years, and that the MLA acknowledged in a conference call that an application had been submitted and said it would be withdrawn and corrected. LawChakra says these are allegations in the complaint and have not been tested. The petition, filed by four petitioners to quash the FIR, argued that they were already accused in the FIR the Jayanagar police registered on 5 October on a complaint by the former MLA Sowmya Reddy (form7-42), that a second FIR over the same exercise was not maintainable, and that the ingredients of forgery and of using forged documents were not made out. The Court issued notice to the complainant, asked the petitioners to serve the petition on the Election Commission's standing counsel and listed the case on 8 January 2027. On 17 November the same judge had stayed the investigation in three other FIRs over Form 7 applications (form7-75).
items.quote: Under these circumstances, prayer for stay of the proceeding is not granted at this juncture. The petitioners shall co-operate for investigation. The respondent-State shall not arrest the petitioners and charge sheet shall not be filed without the leave of the Court.
items.response: The Additional State Public Prosecutor, Anoop Kumar, said the complaint required investigation, and that in earlier cases raising almost the same questions the State had said it would not arrest the petitioners, which would apply here as long as they cooperated with the probe, LawChakra reported. No report carries a statement by the MLA.
items.note: First reading, 24 November 2026, by the courts group's reader, added to this file by the second reader. items.headline: 73.3 lakh left off draft roll, barely 1,000 file fresh forms in Telangana
items.claim: Barely 1,000 of the 73.3 lakh electors left off Telangana's draft roll of 17 August had submitted fresh enumeration forms, The Times of India reported on 25 November. The office of the Chief Electoral Officer told the paper that reports from the districts showed only around 50 to 100 people in each district had come forward. The paper gives 45.1 lakh of those left off as permanently shifted, 11.2 lakh as absent or untraceable, 9.2 lakh as dead and 6.7 lakh as already enrolled elsewhere. The office said the electors in these categories were identified only after house to house visits and due enquiry by booth level officers. Officials told the paper that many electors who found their names missing had applied on Form 6 before the Commission gave them the further opportunity. Booth level officers collect the fresh forms until 30 November, and the final roll is due on 22 December. District reports as of 20 November showed that nearly 99 per cent, or 92 lakh, of the 92.8 lakh electors on the draft who were sent notices had been cleared for the final roll, 60.1 lakh of them with logical discrepancies and 31.8 lakh who could not be matched with earlier rolls. Of the 2,64,87,213 electors on the draft, officials had marked 2,63,96,341 for inclusion in the final roll and 58,772 as ineligible, and decisions were pending in 32,100 cases, 22,958 of them in Hyderabad, against 29 in Rangareddy and 22 in Medchal-Malkajgiri. Across the state 35,934 unmapped electors and 21,885 electors with logical discrepancies were marked ineligible. Rangareddy had the most marked ineligible, 13,493, 11,471 of them unmapped, and Mulugu the highest share, 1.39 per cent of its draft electorate, against 0.22 per cent for the state.
items.quote: The Telangana chief electoral officer’s (CEO) office said reports from districts showed that only around 50 to 100 people in each district has so far come forward to submit fresh enumeration forms.
items.response: The count of fresh forms is rounded, and the paper gives no count for any named district. It does not say how many of the forms were accepted, or how many electors left off the draft applied on Form 6.

The paper's 73.3 lakh is the site's 73,39,235 left off Telangana's draft (states.json), and 2,64,87,213 is the site's 3,38,26,448 before the revision less those left off. Its four categories add to 72.2 lakh, and Deccan Chronicle gave 1,02,294 in a fifth category, other, on 19 November (form7-79). Around 50 to 100 people in each of Telangana's 33 districts would come to about 1,650 to 3,300, more than the paper's barely 1,000, and the paper does not reconcile the two. 2,63,96,341, 58,772 and 32,100 add to 2,64,87,213. 2,63,96,341 is 99.66 per cent of the draft, and the paper prints 99.6%. 58,772 is 0.22 per cent of the draft. 22,958 is 71.5 per cent of 32,100, as the paper says. 35,934 and 21,885 add to 57,819, 953 fewer than the 58,772 marked ineligible, and the paper does not say what the 953 are. The final roll of 22 December and the collection of the forms by 30 November are the Commission's letter of 17 November in process.json. items.headline: Deletion of father’s name from voter list poses hurdle to infant’s birth certificate
items.claim: A two and a half month old infant in Cooch Behar district has been denied a birth certificate as a result of the deletion of her father's name from the roll during the revision, The Hindu reported on 24 November. The girl was born on 9 September at the sub-divisional hospital in Dinhata. The paper reports that when her parents approached the hospital and the panchayat office for the certificate, they were asked to arrange residential verification from the panchayat pradhan or the MLA, that the office of the MLA for Dinhata, Ajoy Roy, refused the father's request for the verification, and that the father was told the certificate could not be issued because his name had been deleted from the roll. The father told the paper that an official from the MLA's office said he was a Bangladeshi national and would first have to register through the National Register of Citizens. He said he has lived in India since his birth, that his house was built by his grandfather, and that he had shown all his documents and was still refused. He said the block development officer of Sahebganj refused a similar request on the same grounds. The paper reports that the names of three of his sisters were also deleted, that the Commission had called them for a hearing citing a logical discrepancy that six other persons had given the name of his father, and that his parents, his wife and an elder sister are on the roll. He has appealed to a tribunal to have his name included. The Association for Protection of Civil Rights said in a statement that birth registration is a statutory obligation, that every child has the right to immediate registration and legal identity under Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, and that a child's right to legal identity must not be linked to the electoral status of her parents, and demanded that the government provide the certificate at once. The Wire carried the same account on 25 November. On 23 November the Supreme Court issued notice on an application asking it to direct the state to withdraw notifications that restrict the welfare benefits of electors deleted in the revision (court-96).
items.quote: An official from the MLA office said that I am a Bangladeshi national and therefore, I would need to get myself first registered through the National Register of Citizens. Why would I do that? I have been living in India since my birth.
items.response: The report carries no statement from the MLA, his office, the panchayat, the block development officer, the hospital or the Chief Electoral Officer. The paper states the refusal by the MLA's office in its own words. The official's remark on nationality and the refusal by the block development officer are the father's account.
items.note: Revised 25 November 2026 from the print page the owner supplied, a photograph of The Hindu's printed report by Senjuti Sengupta, Kolkata, which shows no date. The online version was published at 10:58 pm IST on 24 November 2026 and is for subscribers (isAccessibleForFree false). Its address is kept as the link. items.headline: Delegation of political parties, civil society groups meets Delhi CEO over SIR deletions
items.claim: A delegation of political parties and civil society groups met Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer on Monday, 23 November, and said afterwards that he had accepted their suggestions, Hindustan Times reported on 25 November. The delegation included members of the Aam Aadmi Party, the Communist Party of India, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) and the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist), the activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri, and members of the Voter Adhikar Manch. It said the Chief Electoral Officer accepted that electors whose names were deleted and placed on the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate list of 31 August can be restored by filling an enumeration form and will keep their original serial and EPIC numbers, that he issued directions, and that a standard operating procedure would be released shortly. It asked that electors deleted who had applied afresh on Form 6 after 31 August be given their original EPIC numbers, and said the Chief Electoral Officer assured it this would be considered. On Form 7 it asked that verification be sought from the booth level agent who filed the form, that all Form 7 applications be made public, that notices go to the electors concerned and that decisions follow a fair hearing. It raised incorrect Form 7 filings in Mustafabad, and said it was agreed that cases where a registration officer or assistant registration officer had filed Form 7 to remove a name would be examined again. The talks were about carrying out the Commission's letter of 6 November on another chance for these electors.
items.quote: For voters whose names were deleted and later placed in the ASDD list released on August 31, the CEO accepted a proposal that their voting rights can be restored by filling an enumeration form. They will retain their original voter serial number and EPIC number.
items.response: An official told the paper the meeting went well and that the office would work on the suggestion, and said several suggestions were already in the pipeline and all demands that make the process easier for ordinary voters would be considered. The paper's opening gives the account of what the Chief Electoral Officer accepted as the delegation's, and a later paragraph states the acceptance on the enumeration form in the paper's own words. No statement or standard operating procedure from his office giving it was found.

items.headline: Missing links: Voter revision leaves Maharashtra sex workers in limbo
items.claim: Sex workers in Maharashtra are at risk of being left off the roll because they cannot link a parent's name to the 2002 roll or produce other documents, The Times of India reported on 25 November. The National Network of Sex Workers wrote to the state's Chief Electoral Officer in July asking for special provisions. In one polling booth of Budhwar Peth in Pune, in the Kasba Peth constituency, 200 of 800 residents were flagged during the revision, and the registration officer for Kasba Peth, Vitthal Joshi, told the paper that officials were now looking into the last 49. The sex workers' collective Sangram found only 46 of roughly 660 women in one part of Sangli on the draft roll, and a worker of Aadhar Bahuudeshiya Sanstha in Jalgaon said 85 of roughly 500 members of the community and their relatives in her area had received notices. A peer educator in Jalgaon said many booth level officers had also asked for caste certificates, which are issued in the father's name. The paper reports that officials require a gap of at least 15 years between the ages of a mother and her child, and the peer educator asked how women who gave birth as minors could meet it. The paper reports that in Sangli, Kolhapur and Satara sex workers had gone missing from the rolls or appeared both on the draft and on the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate list. Joshi said special camps had been held at polling stations and civic offices, that where mapping to a parent failed officials placed women in a no linkage category and accepted letters from organisations, statements from landlords on 15 to 30 years of residence and booth level officers' field reports, and that those left off can still apply on Form 6. The final roll is due on 22 December.
items.quote: Where progeny mapping failed, officials placed women under a “no linkage” category, accepting NGO letters, landlord statements confirming 15 to 30 years of residency, and BLO field reports.
items.response: The counts for Sangli and Jalgaon are the organisations' and the paper gives no official count for any of the places. Akshay Jain, chairman of media and communication of the Maharashtra Youth Congress, said he knew several women sex workers and transgender people in the area who had been left off the rolls despite living there for 25 to 35 years, and that the Commission must ensure no vulnerable citizen is disenfranchised in the name of verification.

items.headline: पात्र युवाओं को भी मतदाता सूची में शामिल नहीं किया जा रहा, CEO ने रांची के तमाड़ में होम टू रोल सत्यापन में पकड़ी गड़बड़ी
items.claim: Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, reviewed home to roll verification of the roll at three polling stations of the Tamar Assembly constituency on Tuesday, 24 November, with the registration officer and assistant registration officers, Dainik Jagran reported on 25 November. In a sample survey of 30 houses in two villages and the urban area of Bundu, officials found seven eligible citizens whose names were not yet on the roll, and the paper reports that all seven are young and meet the conditions for registration. He then directed all district election officers and registration officers to run an intensive home to roll verification drive in their constituencies, and to identify and register every eligible citizen who had turned 18 by 1 October 2026. He said it must be ensured that no eligible citizen is left without a name on the roll.

items.outlet: Election Commission of India, letter No. 23/2026-ERS dated 25 November 2026 to the Chief Electoral Officers of 25 states and union territories
items.headline: Special Summary Revision of Electoral Rolls w.r.t. 01.01.2027 as qualifying date
items.claim: The Election Commission directed the Chief Electoral Officers of 25 states and union territories in a letter of 25 November 2026, No. 23/2026-ERS, to identify and rectify probable incorrect or erroneous entries in the particulars of electors during the special summary revision now under way. The existing particulars on the rolls, such as the name, the relation's name or type, the date of birth, the mobile number and the photograph, are to be compared with the information collected during the Special Intensive Revision, and every mismatch is to be flagged for verification and corrective action. For each flagged entry the booth level officer is to visit the elector to verify the particulars and obtain a filled-in Form 8 signed by the elector where one is required, and the assistant registration officer or the registration officer is to decide the application under the prescribed procedure. The letter says that every correction is to be made only through Form 8 signed by the elector and after the prescribed verification and approval, that no change is to be made solely on the basis of automated identification, and that the work is to be done through the booth level officer, assistant registration officer and registration officer modules of ECINet. The 25 are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, Karnataka and Meghalaya. The letter refers to the Commission's letters of 15 October, 4 November and 16 November 2026 on the summary revision in these states and union territories.
items.quote: Since this exercise involves updation of the demographic particulars of electors, all corrections shall be effected only through Form-8, duly signed by the concerned elector and subject to the prescribed verification and approval by the competent authority. No changes shall be made solely on the basis of automated identification.
items.response: The letter gives no count of entries flagged or expected, does not say how such entries arose and sets no date by which the comparison is to be finished. Senior Commission officials told Hindustan Times that the move followed irregularities flagged in the rolls after the revision, and one of them gave as examples one person appearing on the rolls several times and duplicate EPIC numbers. The standfirst of The Hindu's report says it follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final rolls published after the revision.

items.headline: BJP-led Bengal govt links Bharosa scheme benefits to post-SIR voter roll, CAA applications
items.claim: The Government of West Bengal has made inclusion in the final roll published after the 2026 revision a key condition of eligibility for its Bharosa scheme, which is to pay educated unemployed people aged 21 to 45 up to Rs 2,000 a month from 1 January 2027, The New Indian Express reported on 25 November with inputs from PTI. The paper reports the guidelines issued by the state government as saying that people whose cases are pending before the SIR appellate tribunal, or whose applications under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act are under consideration, will also be eligible. The state Cabinet approved the scheme on 23 November. Graduates and people taking or holding vocational certificates from government industrial training institutes are to receive Rs 2,000 a month, and non-graduates and undergraduates Rs 1,500. Applicants must be permanent residents of the state, and the guidelines leave out the self-employed, people in government or private employment, beneficiaries of the Annapurna Yojana and other state social security schemes, and more than two applicants from one family. Persons with disabilities receiving pensions such as the Manabik pension remain eligible. Assistance may be withheld or stopped, after the person concerned is heard, if it was sanctioned on incorrect information or the beneficiary ceases to meet the conditions.
items.quote: Those whose cases are pending before the SIR Appellate Tribunal or whose applications under the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) are under consideration will also be eligible, according to guidelines issued by the state government.
items.response: The report gives no statement from the state government beyond the guidelines, no response from any party and no estimate of how many applicants the condition would affect. The guidelines and any notification of them were not found.
items.note: First reading, 26 November 2026. The New Indian Express, TNIE online desk, with inputs from PTI. Its JSON-LD gives datePublished 2026-11-25T19:02:53Z, and its address carries 25 November. The JSON-LD carries no isAccessibleForFree and the page shows no subscriber marker, and the report was read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 26 November 2026. The paper calls the condition a key eligibility condition, and the item does not say that being on the final roll is required in every case, because the guidelines as reported also admit those with appeals pending and applications under the Act. The application by Prasenjit Bose before the Supreme Court asks for the withdrawal of state notifications restricting the access of deleted electors to welfare benefits (court-96), and the Annapurna Yojana it names is the scheme whose beneficiaries the Bharosa guidelines leave out. The paper's account of the BJP's election result and its link to another report on certificates under the Act are not carried. The item adds no row to the bulk Form 7 table.

items.headline: Howrah Police collect documents from people excluded during SIR; Election office unaware!
items.claim: Police in the Jagacha area of Howrah were collecting personal details and copies of identity documents on Wednesday, 25 November, from residents of Unsani whose names the report says were omitted from the final roll of the revision, Taaza TV reported. Residents told it they were asked for voter identity cards, Aadhaar cards, PAN cards and bank passbooks, and that several declined to hand over copies because no receipt or acknowledgement was given. A sub-inspector said instructions had been sent to all police stations by the state police about two days earlier to collect and forward data on residents left out in the revision, and an official of the district's election office, speaking without being named, said the election administration had no knowledge of any collection of data led by the police. Dainik Jagran reported on 26 November that police stations of the Howrah City Police and the Howrah Rural Police had begun collecting the documents of electors whose cases are pending before the tribunal, asking for copies of Aadhaar and voter identity cards, and that the police said the state police had directed the police stations of every district to verify the documents of electors whose cases are pending before the tribunals. A former CPI(M) councillor, whose own case has been before the tribunal since April, told the paper that collecting documents is the work of the election officials and booth level officers, and that they do not even know of the process. The convener of the Howrah district Left Front, Paresh Pal, wrote to the District Magistrate asking for a meeting on it, and the Left Front asked why the police had been given the work without notice to the public and without a meeting of all parties.
items.quote: Meanwhile, an acting official at the district’s chief electoral office stated anonymously that the election administration had no knowledge of any such police-led data collection exercise.
items.response: Neither report gives the written order or its legal basis, and Taaza TV reports that the officers did not cite either. Neither gives a statement from the state police, the District Magistrate or the Chief Electoral Officer.
items.note: First reading, 26 November 2026. Taaza TV, by Utsav Kumar Verma, read in full from the page text with curl on 26 November 2026. The page shows the date 25 November 2026 and carries no subscriber marker. Its word for the electors is those whose cases are pending before the tribunal after their names were cut from the roll. Jagacha is a police station area of Howrah and Unsani a locality in it. Jagran names the former councillor, and because the report concerns his own pending case he is given by role. Paresh Pal is named as a party office-holder. Taaza TV's line that booth level officers have reportedly said the revision is suspended is not carried, and its sentence on the Supreme Court's directions refers to court-95. Anandabazar Patrika's report on the same collection in Jagacha answered 403 to curl and was not read. The item adds no row to the bulk Form 7 table.

items.headline: Pune: Special Camps On November 28, 29 To Help ASDD Voters Submit SIR Forms
items.claim: The Pune district election administration will hold special camps at every polling station in the district on Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November for electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate to submit their enumeration forms, The Free Press Journal reported on 25 November. The paper gives the schedule of the Commission's letter of 17 November as forms prepared and printed by 18 November, handed out and collected from 18 to 30 November and processed by 10 December, claims and objections decided by 15 December and the final roll published on 22 December. Loksatta reported on 24 November that Thane's District Election Officer, Shrikrishna Panchal, told a press conference on Monday, 23 November, that the enumeration forms of 28,60,266 electors in the district's 18 Assembly constituencies are in the category of electors left off the draft. Of them 2,22,706 are recorded as dead, 17,08,045 as not found at their address or absent, 7,35,144 as permanently shifted and 41,033 for other reasons, and 1,53,338 are recorded as already enrolled. The forms are being sent through booth level officers and by WhatsApp, email and SMS, and the paper gives 30 November as the last date. Electors who had not filed an enumeration form before are to submit Annexure B with it, and electors who moved within the state Annexure C. The district received 1,67,152 applications from 31 August to 13 November, 1,06,149 on Form 6, 360 on Form 6A, 11,093 on Form 7 and 49,550 on Form 8, and the paper reports that inclusion had been completed on 1,30,739 of them and 10,887 were pending.
