items.outlet: The Wire; The Indian Express; The Times of India
items.headline: Bengal Police Are Demanding Documents From Voters Awaiting SIR Tribunal Orders. The CEO Office Doesn't Know Why
items.claim: An order of the West Bengal Police headquarters, No. 1754/DGP(L&O)/26 dated 23 November 2026 and signed by the Director General and Inspector General of Police (Law and Order), asks every police commissioner in the state except Kolkata's and the superintendent of police of every district and police district to examine the data for their jurisdictions on the website of the Civic Research Group, which compiles public data on the adjudication and appeals of the revision by constituency, to analyse it as instructed in a video conference that day and to send a comprehensive report by 30 November, The Wire reported on 27 November from the order, which it has seen. The order's subject is the SIR adjudication and tribunal appeals against exclusion and inclusion across all 294 Assembly constituencies of West Bengal. The Wire reports that the order says nothing about visiting electors, calling them to police stations or collecting their documents, and that police visits to electors whose appeals are pending before the tribunals began in most places on 24 and 25 November, in the districts of Malda, Jalpaiguri, Dakshin Dinajpur, Purba Bardhaman, Bankura, South 24 Parganas, Hooghly, Howrah, Paschim Medinipur, North 24 Parganas and Murshidabad. A checklist of the Kotwali police station in Paschim Medinipur that The Wire has seen asks for each elector's EPIC number, constituency, booth and contact number and whether the elector holds each of six documents, tells the officer to collect a self-attested copy of any the elector has, asks for reports to the District Intelligence Branch by 6 pm every day and sets 28 November for finishing the verification. A second document, in Bengali and headed 'Simplified Check List for Deleted Voters', lists six kinds of proof, among them a land deed from before 1987 in an ancestor's name, a Class X certificate from before 1987 in the elector's or an ancestor's name and an ancestor's name on the rolls of 1971, and The Wire reports that its first line says a deleted voter 'can be considered an Indian citizen' if they can give any one of them. The Indian Express reports that a senior police official, speaking without being named, said a drive began on Tuesday, 24 November, in Jalpaiguri, Uttar Dinajpur, Howrah and East Midnapore and was extended to Murshidabad on Thursday, 26 November. The Times of India reports that sub-inspectors and civic volunteers checked the EPIC cards and family records of appellants at verification points in Murshidabad, Malda, East Burdwan, Jalpaiguri, West Midnapore and other districts on 26 November, with seven verification camps in each block of Jalpaiguri. The Wire reports that on the morning of 27 November booth level officers in at least two constituencies of South 24 Parganas were told by forwarded messages to bring electors under adjudication to the block office with copies of six documents, among them their tribunal application.
items.quote: The data available on the website shall be downloaded, carefully analysed as per instructions given today in Video Conference (VC) and a comprehensive report in respect of the respective jurisdiction shall be submitted to this office positively by 30/11/2026.
items.response: The Additional Chief Electoral Officer, Arindam Niyogi, told The Wire that there was no directive from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, and told The Indian Express that the office had no knowledge of any such drive and did not know whether the Election Commission had asked the police to verify the documents of excluded electors. The Director General of Police, Siddhinath Gupta, told The Indian Express that he could not share the directives and orders his office issues and that he did not know about any forms being filled up, and The Wire reports that he had not answered its questions by the time of publication. The Superintendent of Police of Barasat, J Marcy, told The Times of India that police stations had been tasked with identifying those who had applied to the tribunals and examining how they applied and what documents they submitted, and the Superintendent of Police of Malda, Anupam Singh, said his officers were collecting birth dates on a direction from the Director General and that it had nothing to do with the revision. A senior official of the state administration, speaking without being named, told The Indian Express that the police may verify whether a person is an Indian citizen. The Wire reports that a notice issued in the name of the BJP MLA for Naihati, Sumitro Chatterjee, asked electors whose cases are before a tribunal and who had been called by their police station to go there on 26 or 27 November with their documents, and that his representative said the Election Commission had sent the order through the block and subdivision offices. The CPI(M)'s state secretary, Mohammed Salim, asked under what law the police were asking for the documents, and the Association for Protection of Civil Rights wrote to the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary asking under what authority the police were acting.
items.note: First reading, 27 November 2026. The Wire, by Aparna Bhattacharya, published 27 November 2026 at 2:13 pm IST, read in full through The Wire's CMS API (cms.thewire.in, post 1114744) on 27 November 2026. It quotes the order's number, date, signatory, addressees, subject and three sentences, and the item gives the order as The Wire reports it. The order itself was not seen. The website the order names is the Civic Research Group's (appeal.civicresearch.in), whose public report the site's tribunals page cites (court-70), and The Wire says it has worked with the group in its reporting on the revision and that the group declined to comment. The second address is The Indian Express, by Atri Mitra and Ravik Bhattacharya, published 27 November 2026 at 5:30 am IST (modified 10:24 am), marked free to read (isAccessibleForFree true) and read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl. The Times of India (TNN, published 27 November 2026 at 9:58 am IST, https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kolkata/appealed-to-sir-tribunal-cops-may-knock-on-your-doors-to-verify-documents-election-commission-however-distances-itself-from-the-exercise/articleshow/136202967.cms) was marked free to read and read in full the same way. The three reports name different districts, and each list is attributed. The Indian Express's 'Tuesday' and 'Thursday' are 24 and 26 November, and The Times of India's 'Thursday' is 26 November. The Times of India gives sources as saying the drive runs from 25 to 29 November with daily reports to the superintendent of police in West Midnapore. The item takes the date of the order. The Hindu's report of the Supreme Court hearing is for subscribers and was used only for court-101. The item adds no row to the bulk Form 7 table.

items.headline: Special Drive to Enroll Left Out Electors from Draft Electoral Roll on being marked as ASDD
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer said in a press note dated 26 November that the period for claims and objections, which opened on 31 August, closed on 25 November, and that 3,37,970 Form 6 applications for inclusion, 631 Form 6A applications, 37,038 Form 7 objections seeking deletion and 1,26,241 Form 8 applications, 5,01,880 in all, were received in that period. items.headline: गुरुग्राम में SIR में गायब मिले 4.53 लाख वोटर्स, नाम जुड़वाने के लिए पहुंचे महज 200
items.claim: In Gurugram district's four Assembly constituencies, Gurgaon, Badshahpur, Pataudi and Sohna, 4,53,079 of the 15,55,034 electors on the roll before the revision were not found at their addresses during it, Dainik Jagran reported on 27 November. Of them 30,000 had been verified so far, and only 200 had come forward to apply to have their names added again. The district has 1,504 booth level officers going from house to house to verify them, and the paper gives 30 November as the last date for the verification and for applying to be added again. The paper reports that under the Commission's revised schedule for Haryana claims and objections are to be decided by 15 December and the final roll published on 22 December. The election tahsildar of Gurugram, Rajendra Hooda, told the paper that electors still not found after 30 November were likely to have moved, to have been enrolled at more than one place, so that one entry is deleted, or to have died, and that each elector's status is being verified so that no eligible elector's name is deleted.
items.quote: इनमें से अब तक 30 हजार मतदाताओं का सत्यापन किया जा चुका है। लेकिन, नाम दोबारा जुड़वाने के लिए केवल 200 मतदाता ही आगे आए हैं।

items.headline: Jharkhand achieves 93% completion of SIR electoral roll hearings in 41 assembly constituencies
items.claim: Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, reviewed on Thursday, 26 November, the 40 of the state's 81 Assembly constituencies where hearings on the notices for no mapping and logical discrepancies had progressed least, and directed the registration officers to dispose of every logical discrepancy, no mapping and other case by 30 November, The Times of India and Dainik Jagran reported. The Times of India reports that more than 93% of the hearings had been completed in the other 41 constituencies, and Dainik Jagran gives 93%. He asked officials to identify the reasons for slow progress and to dispose of each case under the rules, and to speed up home to roll verification. For cases still pending he asked the officers concerned to survey and verify them in person and review their status. He directed that during super checking and home to roll verification special efforts be made to enrol every eligible citizen who had turned 18 by 1 October 2026.
items.quote: Reviewing the progress of hearings in 40 assembly constituencies, where the disposal rate has been low, Jharkhand chief electoral officer (CEO) K Ravi Kumar on Thursday directed electoral registration officers (EROs) to achieve 100% disposal of ‘Logical discrepancy’, ‘No mapping’ and ‘Others’ cases by Nov 30.
items.response: Neither report gives a count of hearings held or pending, names the constituencies on either side of the line or gives a count of electors found ineligible. The Times of India reported from the office's data that 18,425 cases had been marked ineligible by 21 November (form7-87).

items.headline: NPCC urges comprehensive SIR
items.claim: The president of the Nagaland Pradesh Congress Committee and Lok Sabha member, Supongmeren Jamir, and its working president, Khrieti, met Nagaland's Chief Electoral Officer, Bhagyashree Banayat, on 26 November to discuss the revision, The Morung Express reported from the party's press statement of that day. The statement as the paper reports it says that during the meeting it was learnt that about 1.57 lakh electors had been deleted from the rolls and that about 25% of them had so far been covered by the revision, and that the exercise was expected to continue until 22 December. The Nagaland Tribune reports that the delegation was told this. The party asked the Election Department for a more detailed and comprehensive revision so that every elector whose name had been deleted, or who remained uncovered, had an adequate chance to be included, The Morung Express reports. The meeting followed a march by the party and its Kohima District Congress Committee.
items.quote: During the meeting, it was learnt that approximately 1.57 lakh voters had been deleted from the electoral rolls, of which around 25% had been covered by the revision process so far.
items.response: The account of what the delegation was told is the party's, and neither report gives a statement from the Chief Electoral Officer. Neither says what being covered by the revision means, whether an enumeration form handed out or returned or a name added back.
